status: built 2026-10-08 (tools/tm_gate.py, pack cobblers_tm_gate, world-local); NOT run in game: experiments/EXP-067-tm-recipe-gate
decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'Gate the recipes by badge.' Each crafted TM unlocks at the same badge as its shelf line: crafting stays the cheap route, but no earlier than the shelf (docs/research/DROP_RATE_CONSUMERS.md 3.3: with alpha gems 16 of the 23 income-gated shelf TMs were craftable before their shelf price was affordable)

mechanism.rung: configuration + datapack + functions (CLAUDE.md principle 6): the vanilla gamerule doLimitedCrafting, the vanilla recipe book, recipe advancements and /recipe. No mod, no scripting layer
mechanism.why_not_cheaper: Cobblemon native: no per-player recipe hook (TMCraft TMs are vanilla crafting_shapeless / crafting_shaped recipes, read from tmcraft-1.4.19+1.8.0.jar data/tmcraft/recipe/). Addon: TMCraft has no crafting hook or config (its only gamerule is consumeMoveItemOnUse, kiwiapollo/tmcraft/gamerule/ModGameRule.class). Fabric resource conditions (the Beast Ball's rung) act at load, server-wide, and cannot read a player
mechanism.verified_from_jar: Minecraft 1.21.1 (client jar 1.21.1-0.19.5, official names, intermediary-1.21.1 for the mapping), read 2026-10-08: RecipeCraftingHolder (crk / class_1732) default setRecipeUsed(Level, ServerPlayer, RecipeHolder) (method_7665) allows a recipe when recipe.isSpecial() || !gamerules.getBoolean(doLimitedCrafting) || player.getRecipeBook().contains(recipe). Its ONLY caller in the jar is CraftingMenu.slotChangedCraftingGrid (cqm / class_1714 method_17399), used by the crafting table and the inventory's 2x2 grid. Furnaces, smithing, the stonecutter and the Crafter block do not call it. doLimitedCrafting defaults to false (GameRules dcs.w, iconst_0)
mechanism.what_it_does_to_every_other_recipe: under doLimitedCrafting a grid recipe a player has not unlocked cannot be crafted at all. So the pack never relies on each recipe's own unlock: on a player's first tick under a new plan, tm_gate/sync runs `recipe give @s *` (every recipe the server loaded, vanilla, Cobblemon and every mod) and then takes back only the gated recipes of the badges that player does not hold. Nothing is stranded for anyone; the sweep (`python tools/tm_gate.py sweep`) counts what WOULD be stranded without that give
mechanism.sync_key: the plan's hash (every loaded recipe id and every gated recipe with its badge) is the score cobblers.tmgate a synced player carries: a new mod, a changed badge or a new TM recipe changes the hash at the next prepare, and every player re-syncs on their next tick
mechanism.earning: one advancement per badge, cobblers:tm_gate/earn/<flag>, minecraft:tick with the player holding cobblers:flag/<flag> (tools/progression_pack.py), rewards the function tm_gate/give/<flag>: `recipe give` of that badge's gated recipes. A sync revokes it for every badge the player lacks, so a revoked flag re-earns
mechanism.unlock_advancements: every loaded advancement whose rewards.recipes names a gated recipe (TMCraft's recipes/misc/tm_*, vanilla's and Carved Wood's crafter unlocks, Tom's crafting terminal's) is written back at its own path closed (fabric:load_conditions that never pass, the tools/key_ball.py form), else holding an ingredient would unlock the recipe early

gated.why: every TMCraft TM recipe the server loads is one of these two types (805 of them, read from the jar and COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31's added recipes). The 929 to_cobblemon_tm_* conversions (a TMCraft TM into a Cobblemon TM of the same move) are not gated: they need the TM already. The smelting recipes into legacy_* items are not crafting-grid recipes and doLimitedCrafting does not reach them

badge_rule.shelf: a TM with a counter line in data/markets.json carrying gate_badge B (stock or held_stock, price_rule income_gate) unlocks at cobblers:flag/gymB_cleared. This is the owner's rule, and wins over the rule below
badge_rule.unlisted: max(type_badge, grade_badge). type_badge: the lowest badge whose leader's first-win TM pool (data/progression.json first_win_rewards, the active series) holds a TM of the same gem type; a type no leader teaches (bug, flying, fighting, ghost, dragon, dark, steel, ice, fairy) takes the LAST leader's badge (8), never minimum_badge. grade_badge: the lowest shelf badge among shelf TMs whose blank disc is at least as high a grade as this TM's (grade_order). So an unlisted TM is never craftable before the shelf sells a TM of its type, nor before the shelf sells a TM of its disc grade
badge_rule.why: both halves are read from the shelf and the leaders' pools, so the rule reproduces every shelf line's badge (tools/tm_gate.py reports any that it does not). The first version defaulted a type no leader teaches to minimum_badge (1) and relied on the grade half to hold it back; but all four badge-1 shelf TMs (Bide, Headbutt, Rock Slide, Rock Tomb) are gold discs, so copper, iron and gold all map to badge 1 and 169 TMs of those nine types, Shadow Ball among them, unlocked before Brock. The owner, 2026-10-08: 'SHADOW BALL AT BADGE 1 IS WRONG ... something in the derivation is off.' A type no leader teaches is now placed at the last leader's badge: the only badge the data can show is not early. Grade alone ignores that the shelf is laid out by gym type (Earthquake, diamond, at badge 8). TMCraft's disc grade is its own power tier: copper is one copper ingot, netherite needs a netherite ingot
badge_rule.owner_review: a balance judgement with no runnable check. With the no-leader types at the last leader, the snapshot of 2026-10-05 places 802 TMs at {1: 134, 2: 23, 3: 47, 4: 39, 5: 78, 6: 65, 7: 89, 8: 327}: the 300 TMs of the nine types all wait for badge 8 (they were at 1: 169, 3: 47, 5: 54, 7: 30). The owner may place those types earlier by naming a badge per type; the derivation alone cannot

devices.items_are: fnmatch patterns on a recipe's result id. carved_wood:<wood>_crafter is Carved Wood's own crafter block (CWCrafterBlock, beside a CrafterBlockEntityAccessor mixin), made by its per-wood shaped recipes; carved_wood:oak_crafter makes a plain minecraft:crafter
devices.vanilla_why: the vanilla jar's own ids (data/minecraft/recipe/crafter.json and data/minecraft/advancement/recipes/redstone/crafter.json in 1.21.1), gated and closed even when the build cannot read a vanilla jar (Carved Wood overrides both at the same paths, so the sweep sees them through it today)
devices.badge: the highest badge any gated TM needs (computed)
devices.why: a crafting device that never asks the recipe book crafts every TM for anyone. The Crafter (vanilla 1.21.1 CrafterBlock looks the recipe up with no player) and Tom's Storage's crafting terminal (toms_storage_fabric-1.21-2.3.0.jar CraftingTerminalBlockEntity calls RecipeManager.getRecipeFor (method_8132) and nothing that reads doLimitedCrafting or the recipe book) are bypasses, read from the jars 2026-10-08. Their own crafting recipes are gated like a TM, at the last TM badge. Carved Wood's carved_wood:wooden_crafter is a SPECIAL recipe (CrafterRecipe extends class_1852, CustomRecipe: isSpecial, so doLimitedCrafting never applies) that makes a minecraft:crafter from mixed crafting tables; it is closed, and the per-wood shaped crafter recipes still make one. Sophisticated Core's crafting upgrade calls method_7665 and obeys the gamerule
devices.owner_review: this withholds the Crafter and the crafting terminal until the last TM badge, for every player. Set enforced false to give them back and accept that either one crafts any TM
devices.owner_decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'DEVICES: keep them gated at badge 8.' enforced stays true

regivers.found: COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31.zip data/cobbleverse/function/starter_pack.mcfunction runs `recipe give @s *`; it is the reward of data/cobblemon/advancement/root.json in the same pack, whose one criterion is {"trigger": "cobblemon:pick_starter"} (read 2026-10-08). So every player who picked a starter already holds every recipe, TMs included, and a player who picks one after the gate synced them would get every TM back
regivers.answer: an advancement of ours on the same trigger, cobblers:tm_gate/resync/<n>, resets the player's cobblers.tmgate score and revokes itself: the next tick re-syncs them after the starter pack has run, whichever reward ran first

does_not_cover: Cobblemon 1.8's own TM Machine (cobblemon:tm_machine) prints native TMs from data/cobblemon/tms/*.json (335 moves: 128 cobblemon:default, always offered; 206 cobblemon:unlockable; 1 cobblemon:advancement), from gems: Earthquake is 10 ground gems, soft sand and a diamond. It is a block-entity menu, not the recipe book, so this gate does not touch it. Read from the jar 2026-10-08: ObtainMethod.matches (PlayerHasAdvancementObtainMethod's per-player check) has no caller in Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar, and only the client's TechnicalMachine.filterTms filters the list. Decided, the owner, 2026-10-08: 'THE TM MACHINE: leave it ungated and accept it as the gem route.' It stays ungated: a player with the gems can print a native TM of any default move before its badge, by design
a crafted TM is an item: a player who holds the badge can craft one and hand it to a player who does not
a TM from loot, a trade or a counter is not a crafted TM; the shelf has its own gate (its price)
TMCraft's Move Tutor Table and Pokemon Breeder Table, and its tutor_* and egg_* items, are code, not recipes: not read
a world that had the pack removed keeps doLimitedCrafting true (a gamerule is saved with the world): run cobblers:tm_gate/off first. Every player keeps the recipes the last sync gave
a recipe a mod adds at runtime in code rather than as a data file is not in the sweep; `recipe give @s *` still gives it, so it is never stranded, only uncounted

the world's own datapacks folder is not read by the sweep (no world is read): a world-local pack's recipes are given by `recipe give @s *` but not counted, and a world-local pack's TM recipe would not be gated
